title: Grafana dashboard (kubestream subset)
description: Structural contract for the dashboards shipped in deploy/grafana/. Grafana publishes no stable, self-contained JSON Schema for a dashboard — its own model is a Go/TypeScript type that changes shape between minor releases — so this is a deliberately curated subset: the fields a dashboard must get right to import cleanly and to stay reviewable, and nothing else. Unknown properties are allowed everywhere so a dashboard exported from a newer Grafana still validates; what is pinned is that the fields we do rely on exist and are well formed.

uid.description: Stable identifier. Pinned in the file so re-importing updates the dashboard in place instead of creating a second copy, and so docs can deep-link to it.

schemaVersion.description: Grafana's own dashboard-model version. Floored at 36 (Grafana 9) because everything below it predates the panel options this dashboard uses.

datasourceRef.description: Every datasource reference goes through the dashboard's own datasource variable. A hard-coded uid would import as a broken panel on any Grafana but the one the dashboard was exported from. Two datasource types are shipped: the operator-health dashboard reads Prometheus (the operator's own metrics), while the product dashboards read the ClickHouse the operator writes to. Which one a target belongs to decides what a target must carry — see the conditional branches on `target`.

target.description: One query. A target carries either PromQL (`expr`) or SQL (`rawSql`) depending on its datasource type, which is why the requirement is conditional rather than a flat list: requiring both would reject every dashboard, and requiring neither would let a target that queries nothing validate.

expr.description: PromQL. Non-empty here; that it parses, and that every metric it names is one the operator actually exports, is asserted by test/observability.

rawSql.description: ClickHouse SQL against the frozen v1 schema. Non-empty here; that it parses and reads only frozen columns is asserted by test/queries, which runs every shipped query against a real ClickHouse built from the shipped DDL alone.

editorType.description: The ClickHouse plugin's editor mode. Pinned to `sql` on every shipped target: the alternative, `builder`, stores a structured query the plugin re-renders into SQL, which would put the actual query out of reach of review and of the test that executes it.

format.description: The ClickHouse plugin's numeric result-format enum: 0 time series, 1 table, 2 logs, 3 trace. It is redundant with `queryType` in current plugin versions and both are written, so an import against a plugin that honours only one of them still reads the query the same way.

description.description: Required, not optional. A panel whose meaning is not written down is a panel an on-call operator has to guess at; the description is the panel's documentation and is where the 'why' of each metric lives.
